styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny window-like fixture, roughly one tile in size, with pale blue panes and a white frame. It has no roof, walls or door, so it is not a whole building and does not match the reference kind. The references are full houses with scalloped roof tiles, timber framing, plaster speckle and per-stone shading, each with about 5-6 steps per material. The candidate shows only about 3 lightness steps and has no roof or wall texture. The measured facts (13 visible tones per tile, 0% near-flat, 0% near-neutral dark edges) are on par with the references, but a single small tile cannot be compared to a full building, and the numbers do not offset the missing structure. Dark edge pixels are tinted rather than neutral, but there are too few of them to judge the outline reliably, so I report 'mixed'. Fail: the piece is the wrong kind and far less developed than the references.
